title: The Ass, the Fox, and the Lion
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: An Ass and a Fox went into partnership and sallied out to forage for food together. They hadn't gone far before they saw a Lion coming their way, at which they were both dreadfully frightened. But the Fox thought he saw a way of saving his own skin, and went boldly up to the Lion and whispered in his ear, "I'll manage that you shall get hold of the Ass without the trouble of stalking him, if you'll promise to let me go free." The Lion agreed to this, and the Fox then rejoined his companion and contrived before long to lead him by a hidden pit, which some hunter had dug as a trap for wild animals, and into which he fell. When the Lion saw that the Ass was safely caught and couldn't get away, it was to the Fox that he first turned his attention, and he soon finished him off, and then at his leisure proceeded to feast upon the Ass.
Betray a friend, and you'll often find you have ruined yourself.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why do the Ass and the Fox go out together?
options: To search for a new home
To settle a dispute between them
To forage for food as partners
To escape from a nearby farm

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Ass and the Fox see coming their way?
options: A Lion
A pack of wolves
A group of hunters
A herd of other asses

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox whisper to the Lion?
options: That the Ass is dangerous and should be avoided
That he wants to join the Lion's hunting pack
That the Ass has already spotted the Lion
That he can help the Lion catch the Ass in exchange for his own freedom

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Fox lead the Ass into danger?
options: By pushing him off a steep cliff
By leading him to a hidden pit dug as a trap for wild animals
By tricking him into a locked cage
By leaving him alone in the Lion's path

questions.prompt: According to the passage, whom does the Lion attack first once the Ass is trapped?
options: The Ass
Neither; he waits for both to weaken
The Fox
A different animal that happened to pass by

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Lion do after dealing with the Fox?
options: He proceeds at his leisure to feast upon the Ass
He releases the Ass as promised
He leaves both animals and walks away
He shares his catch with the Fox's family

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Lion have no reason to keep his promise to the Fox?
options: The Fox never actually delivered on his part of the bargain
The Lion never truly agreed to the Fox's plan in the first place
The Fox demanded a reward the Lion could not provide
Once the Ass is trapped, the Lion no longer needs the Fox's help at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Fox fail to consider when striking his bargain with the Lion?
options: That the Ass might overhear his whispered plan
That betraying his partner leaves him with nothing to stop the Lion from turning on him next
That the pit might not be strong enough to hold the Ass
That the Lion might refuse the deal outright

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Ass and Fox "went into partnership"?
options: They competed against each other for food
They belonged to the same owner
They agreed to work together toward a shared goal
They had known each other since birth

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: Betraying someone who trusts you can end up destroying you as well
Lions are always more dangerous than they first appear
Foxes are naturally more cunning than any other animal
Partnerships between different kinds of animals never last long

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how do the Ass and Fox feel when they first see the Lion?
options: Curious but calm
Angry and ready to fight
Confident they can outrun him
Dreadfully frightened

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox ask the Lion to promise in return for his help?
options: To share the meal equally
To let him go free
To spare the Ass as well
To protect him from hunters

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who originally dug the pit that traps the Ass?
options: The Fox himself
A group of farmers
Some hunter
The Lion, long before this story

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Fox go "boldly up to the Lion" rather than fleeing?
options: He believes striking a private bargain is his best chance of surviving the encounter
He is confident he can defeat the Lion in a fight
He wants to warn the Lion about the hidden pit
He hopes the Ass will protect him from the Lion

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the order of the Lion's attacks (Fox first, then Ass) suggest about the value of the Fox's bargain?
options: The Lion always intended to spare the Fox completely
The Fox's bargain was honored in full by the Lion
The Ass had somehow bargained for the Fox's safety too
The bargain protected the Fox for only as long as he was still useful to the Lion

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Fox "contrived" to lead the Ass to the pit?
options: He stumbled upon it by pure accident
He planned and managed it deliberately
He was ordered to do it by the Lion
He warned the Ass about it beforehand

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Fox and an Ass work together to escape a Lion
An Ass tricks a Lion into freeing the Fox
A Fox betrays his partner to a Lion, then is killed by the Lion himself
A Lion spares both the Ass and the Fox out of gratitude
